blocks.text: SAN FRANCISCO, Agusan del Sur — Where chainsaws and slash-and-burn farming once tore through ancestral frontiers, provincial leaders are now betting that specialty coffee can brew an economic turnaround for isolated mountain villages. On Wednesday, local officials led by Agusan del Sur 2nd District Rep. Adolph Edward Plaza climbed the winding slopes of Barangay Padiay, Sibagat town, to inspect a 45-hectare model plantation—the pilot of an envisioned 100-hectare commercial coffee corridor. The initiative aims to clone the success of neighboring Bukidnon, which has gained national acclaim and premium cupping awards over the past decade for its specialty Arabica coffee. READ: The […]...
